haiku-low.q1: It lists rejected events with a reason in the response and accepts the rest. The 202 is returned only after every accepted event in the batch is acknowledged by the log.
haiku-low.q2: It resends the same batch with the same event_ids, backing off exponentially from 1 s up to 5 minutes.
haiku-low.q3: The first copy the collector receives wins. Later copies are dropped from events_clean, though all copies stay in the archive.
haiku-low.q4: Tuesday. Its partition and replay use the UTC day of received_at, never the client timestamp.
haiku-low.q5: In the existing key-value store with per-key TTL. Each event_id key stores (log partition, offset). Entries expire after an 8-day TTL set at first sight, never refreshed.
haiku-low.q6: The dedup consumer stops and retries. It never skips the duplicate check, so processing waits until the store recovers.
haiku-low.q7: Each load writes rows and its (log partition, start offset, end offset) in one transaction. Recorded batches are skipped on retry, unrecorded ones reloaded, and offset-valued KV entries keep the winner.
haiku-low.q8: It reads the raw archive for D-8 through D plus pinned enrichment data. Rebuilt events go to a staging table, validated, then atomically swapped into events_clean.
haiku-low.q9: It orders each event_id's copies by (log partition, offset). The first copy wins, later copies within 8 days of the winner are dropped, and only D's winners are kept.
haiku-low.q10: events_clean is left untouched. Rerunning is safe because the job is idempotent per day. A bad swap is undone by swapping the backup back in.
haiku-low.q11: Only closed days, with no other replay holding the lock, and the archive covering D plus the 8 days before. D must be at most about 82 days old.
haiku-low.q12: Not decided. One isolated stage after dedup will either drop suspected bots or keep them with an is_suspected_bot flag. The archive keeps every event.

sonnet.q1: It rejects the malformed events (missing event_id/device_id, or over 32 KB), lists them with reasons in the response, and continues with the rest. It returns 202 only after every accepted event in the batch has been acknowledged by the log; if any append fails it returns 5xx.
sonnet.q2: It resends the same batch with the same event_ids, backing off exponentially from 1 s up to 5 minutes. (Mobile SDK buffers unacknowledged events up to 7 days; clients never retry events the collector rejected.)
sonnet.q3: The first copy received (earliest by log partition offset) wins and lands in events_clean; later copies are dropped, provided they arrive within the 8-day dedup window. A copy arriving after the TTL expires (past 8 days) would not be caught by the live KV state. The raw copies all stay in the archive.
sonnet.q4: Tuesday's partition and replay. The day is the UTC day of received_at (00:10 Tuesday), never the client timestamp.
sonnet.q5: In the KV store, keyed by event_id, with value (log partition, offset), set via atomic set-if-absent. Entries are removed by a per-key TTL of 8 days, set at first sight and never refreshed.
sonnet.q6: The dedup consumer stops and retries; it never skips the check. Events still get accepted by the collector and written to the log and archive; they just are not loaded into events_clean until KV recovers (consumer lag builds).
sonnet.q7: Load transaction appends rows and records the batch's (partition, start offset, end offset) in the control table atomically in one transaction, so a crash leaves either both or neither. On retry a recorded batch is skipped and an unrecorded one is reloaded. Also, the KV entry stores the event's offset, so on reprocessing an event whose stored offset equals its own is still treated as the winner rather than a duplicate.
sonnet.q8: It reads only the archive (raw files in object storage, D-8 through D) plus pinned enrichment data. Rebuilt events are written to a staging table, not events_clean, until validation passes and the atomic partition swap.
sonnet.q9: It reads the archive for D-8 through D, orders copies of each event_id by (log partition, offset), applies the live rule (first copy wins; a later copy is dropped if within 8 days of the current winner), and keeps only D's winners. Events whose first copy arrived on an earlier day are thus dropped, as live did.
sonnet.q10: events_clean is untouched (replay writes only to staging until swap; gate/validation failure or crash changes nothing). The operator can safely rerun, as the job is idempotent per day. (If a bad replay was swapped in later, roll back by swapping in the 14-day backup.)
sonnet.q11: Only closed days (closed by the day-close job at 02:00 UTC on D+1), with no other replay holding the lock for D, and where the archive covers D and the 8 days before it, so D must be at most about 82 days old.
sonnet.q12: Undecided (open question). Classification sits in one isolated stage after dedup and enrichment (step 7). Option 1 drops bots from events_clean (still recorded in dedup state); option 2 keeps them with a flag column such as is_suspected_bot. Either way the archive keeps every event.
